0.content:
Yoimiya's father and the previous owner of Naganohara Fireworks. Since an accident his hearing has been poor, so customers must repeat themselves, and he cheerfully answers questions nobody asked. He launches into long tales of how people first learned that ground minerals burn in colours. As a child Yoimiya took his constant smile as agreement with everything she said; when she learned the truth she kept talking anyway, because it makes him happy and keeps him from being lonely. He found her discarded Vision in the storeroom and taught her its worth. Her favourite of his stories: a firework's last sparks become rain and snow, nourish the land, and one day rise into the sky again.

He still minds the shop and the goods while she runs errands. In a daily commission he hands her new test fireworks to the Traveler, calling her "my little girl" and a "real good tinkerer". When the Tenryou Commission raided the house for Sakujirou, he tried to stop them by calling the place a fire hazard. Before her Sumeru trip he worried with her mother about her going so far.

1.comment: Yoimiya: Naganohara Fireworks and the formula slips
1.content:
The Naganohara family shop in Hanamizaka, Inazuma City, and the namesake of the Naganohara Fireworks Show. It began over a century ago when the Yashiro Commission ordered a commemorative display, and has since become a festival where everyone lights their own fireworks before the owner's grand finale. Every customer who orders a commemorative firework receives a note readable only by the family. It records the formula, so whether ten or a hundred years pass, the Naganohara can make exactly the same firework again. Yoimiya calls the family "keepers of the gate" to past memories. The shop also sells toys and knickknacks. Its customers are mostly regulars, and the family works "so that we won't let everyone down".

Under the Sakoku Decree the shop exported in secret through Beidou; much of Liyue's Lantern Rite stock came from it. Yoimiya also handed out slips to Hanamizaka children and their parents as part of a game. The fire brigade has lectured her many times, and the Tenryou Commission has been angered by fireworks set off on its property.

2.content:
The Yashiro Commission and its shrine maidens run Inazuma's festivals, and Yoimiya creates their spectacle, so the two have worked together for years. Ayaka asked for the Shogun's emblem in Yoimiya's first show and got it cleverly hidden in the display. Yoimiya says Ayaka always lets her finish and answers seriously, unlike people in the other Commissions; "ladylike" was made for her. After a late-night festival meeting Yoimiya suggested a public bath, and Ayaka went red, since noble ladies cannot use them. Ayaka defends fireworks against public-order objections. In 2.0 she sent the Traveler to Yoimiya to free Master Masakatsu.

In 4.3 (limited event, Roses and Muskets) the two toured Fontaine together with Kamisato Ayato for Furina's film. They dived together, Yoimiya clutching Ayaka's hand on her first breath underwater, and planned to hunt for a Beryl Conch. In 5.4 (limited) Ayaka helped Yoimiya and Sayu's festival game team.

3.comment: Yoimiya: The Vision Hunt Decree and Master Masakatsu
3.content:
Under the Vision Hunt Decree, Hanamizaka craftsman Master Masakatsu made counterfeit Visions for the resistance, and Yoimiya kept her own Vision thanks to them. When the Traveler first arrived at Naganohara Fireworks, Tenryou samurai were confiscating a man's Vision. Yoimiya pulled the Traveler aside; the samurai left with a fake she had swapped in. Masakatsu had since been arrested. Yoimiya had been thinking of breaking him out but did not want to embarrass Ayaka, so she joined the Traveler. She led them in by a way she had scouted beforehand and set off a firework "gift" to draw the guards while they freed the tortured craftsman; Kujou Sara let them go for the sake of his health.

In 2.1 (Omnipresence Over Mortals), Thoma and Ayaka's plan to expose Kujou Takayuki needed a diversion. Yoimiya handed over an extra-large firework too powerful to test anywhere, with cheerful safety advice ("What's the worst that could happen!"). Its blast covered Sayu's theft of the Tenryou Commission's reports to the Shogun. In a voice line the Raiden Shogun asks who set off fireworks on Tenryou Commission property and guesses it was her.

4.content:
To Hanamizaka's children Yoimiya is a heroic big sister who always has a solution. She plays timeless games with them and hunts shiny trinkets with them. She protects their fantasies: she told them the Great Mujina Youkai is cute, mischievous and harmless, and gave them firework "weapons" to scare it off. She refused to debunk a tale whose real reasons she did not know. An old folksong about rainbows turning into wish-fireworks led the children to bring her "shiny" treasures. She makes each child a firework of their own for creek pebbles or shell shards, and takes them to return anything expensive to its owner. She wants them to have a happy time even during the lockdown.

Named children include Matsuzaka, Iwao and Saika; in Nod-Krai she had Aino make them a toy fish pot so they would not have to keep real fish alive. Her ascension lines imagine introducing herself to them as a hero: "Evil begone! Justice prevails!"

5.content:
Itto is as popular with the children as she is, and every play session turns into a showdown: a bowl of ramen soup in one go, sour plums without a grimace, with the children cheering and betting. She "can't let him beat me". She was surprised to learn his gang was real and he was not just idle. He buys her custom knickknacks to challenge his "nemesis" Kujou Sara. He grumbles that her fireworks and toys steal his thunder, and insists anyone shorter than him is a kid who should side with him.

She promised fireworks for his 4.6 music festival (limited event) and delivered, critiqued his rock music with Thoma and decided the absent dog might mean the world was at peace.

6.comment: Yoimiya: Dreamlike Timelessness: Sakujirou and Keisuke
6.content: Yoimiya's first Story Quest act (2.0), during preparations for the Naganohara Fireworks Show. An old customer, Sakujirou, born in Inazuma, smuggled himself home and was wanted by the Tenryou Commission; she hid him and asked her friend Kouichi to build a boat. From Konda Village's Imatani couple she learned that Sakujirou had once quarrelled with their son Keisuke, his childhood best friend and now a Tenryou officer, because Sakujirou wanted to see the world. When Keisuke raided the shop, she broke through a blockade, then challenged Keisuke to a duel: if she lost she would be arrested; if she won the two must talk. She won. Keisuke let Sakujirou leave and lit their old shared firework himself; Sakujirou, watching from the boat, recognised it and wept. She watched the show with the Traveler from a cliff on Amakane Island and gave them the formula slip for a golden firework she had her father make for them.

7.comment: Yoimiya: Star-Pickers' Passage: Sumeru and the Aranara
7.content: Yoimiya's second act (3.7). With the Sakoku Decree gone, she set out to see Teyvat's greatest meteor shower for inspiration, carrying dozens of wishes written by Inazumans. The Traveler took her to Sumeru, her first time abroad. Nahida explained that meteor showers cannot be predicted and offered a kind "lie": a dream shower made with the Aranara's help. In Sumeru City Yoimiya befriended Avin, a girl who had lost the use of her legs to illness and was losing her happy memories. The Aranara Arapurva saw that Yoimiya had "not yet grown up" and trusted her. In the dream Avin ran again and reunited with her Aranara friend Arashani, and the stars rose from the ground. Yoimiya knew it was a dream and was grateful anyway: dreams are experiences that cannot be relived. Avin's new dream was to travel to Inazuma on her own to watch a fireworks show. Yoimiya gave the Traveler an Aranara carving as a promise of support.

8.comment: Yoimiya: The Raiden Shogun and eternity
8.content: Yoimiya worships Ei and once hid the Shogun's crest in a fireworks display meant for her eyes from the Tenshukaku. Yet she thinks fireworks are the furthest thing from the Shogun's "eternity", and that a being who holds eternity cannot see why fleeting mortals treasure brief beauty. The Shogun, asked about her, calls her a manufacturer of fleeting illusions enamoured of fantasy, "but a subject of mine nonetheless". Joking about her Vision, Yoimiya is glad it was never "taken back by our dear Archon".

9.content: Since Inazuma's lockdown Beidou has carried Naganohara fireworks out of the country, including many used at Liyue's Lantern Rite, although exports were forbidden: "How can there be festivals without fireworks?" To surprise her, Yoimiya launched a huge boat-shaped firework as the Crux departed. The sailors thought one of their ships had flown off; Beidou called it exactly what a pleasant surprise should be. The shop also sells curios Beidou imported, reworked by Yoimiya.

10.comment: Yoimiya: Kujou Sara and the Tenryou Commission
10.content: Fire-safety concerns often get Yoimiya taken to the Tenryou Commission for a lecture. Kujou Sara is the most reasonable there: she hears her out first and admits it when she is right. When Yoimiya is wrong, she gets Thoma to help her apologise. Sara grants her fireworks are spectacular but reminds herself not to be captivated by something transient. In 2.0 Sara caught Yoimiya's group freeing Masakatsu and let them go. Yae Miko enjoyed hearing that fireworks set off "all over the place" had turned the Kujou Clan purple with rage.

11.content: Thoma finds her easy to get along with, "super straightforward", and hands out coupons for her fireworks. She admires how his talk, however roundabout, always comes to a single purpose, quite unlike hers, and asks his help whenever she cannot settle something. She mentioned in 3.7 that he once sent the family wine from Mondstadt.

12.content: Yoimiya wants to take Sayu to festivals and introduce her to new friends, since she "always looks a little down". Sayu complains that Yoimiya calls her "little tanuki" and really just wants a ninjutsu performance during the fireworks show. During the limited-time Mikawa Flower Festival event (5.4), Yoimiya rushed to see a rumoured youkai showdown and met the bake-danuki Kichiboushi. She then teamed up with Sayu to design a festival game, "The Most Wonderful Bunshin Phantasm: Mujina Body Doubles to the Rescue!", which was Sayu's idea. Yoimiya had always wanted to go to a festival with Sayu.

13.comment: Yoimiya: Klee and the Irodori Festival
13.content: Yoimiya once heard of a Mondstadt child who makes bombs and called her a possible genius, while worrying that Mondstadt lets children play with explosives. During the limited-time 2.6 event Hues of the Violet Garden, Klee came to Inazuma and met her. Fireworks were banned in the city during the Irodori Festival, to Yoimiya's quiet disappointment. Instead she helped Klee paint Dodoco's adventure as a picture book and pleaded with the Yae Publishing House to print it. She recalled crying as a child when her father forgot a festival, and refused to let Klee feel that way. Yae Miko allowed a half-size print.

14.comment: Yoimiya: Nod-Krai holiday: Aino and Ineffa
14.content: Travelers' Tales Anecdotes (6.4): in the fireworks off-season Yoimiya holidayed in Nod-Krai for inspiration. She photographed Hiisi Island's colours for reference and bought gifts for her parents. Hearing that Aino is a child who lived alone with machines she built, she wondered how many nights Aino had spent by herself, and resolved to make sure she had a great time. She borrowed Nasha Town's crafting station and made Aino fireworks, temari, a kite and a spinning top. In return Aino built a "Wibbly Wobbly Fishie Pot" for Hanamizaka's children. "Big Sis Yoimiya" and Aino played tops until they fell asleep on the sofa, and Ineffa covered them with a blanket. Ineffa judged that Aino had made a new friend.

15.content: During a limited-time 6.2 event, Yoimiya visited Mondstadt during the International Cross Country Challenge; she had never been anywhere so cold. She had her first snowball fight and built her first snowman, and she met Natlanese fans of The Soulblazer Saga comics, including Varesa. She made and gave the Traveler a stand of the character Fietena. Her real purpose was dandelions, light enough to make firework pictures linger. She treated the Natlanese adventurer Bold Bang Bouldern's injured back with a gunpowder-warmed compress and, with the Knights' permission, hunted stray monsters as a "free mercenary". She found Mondstadt so relaxed she could fall asleep anywhere, and thought it could use a few more festivals.

16.content: During the limited-time 4.3 event, Yoimiya came to Fontaine with Ayaka and Ayato for Furina's film "The Two Musketeers". She was not cast, so she volunteered as director's assistant, fetching coffee and rigging lights ("kinda like designing a fireworks show"). She marvelled at the buildings, food and her first underwater breath. At the wrap party she lured the producer Morris to a dark warehouse "to fetch fireworks". It was a scene staged by Captain Chevreuse, in which Yoimiya played the victim, to draw a murder confession from him. Chevreuse thanked her for her performance.

17.content: Limited-time events, canon but not universally known. In Akitsu Kimodameshi (3.3) she could partner the Traveler in the Test of Courage, hoping to meet a real evil spirit; she was disappointed when it was only a cat. In the Iridescent Arataki music festival (4.6) she kept her word to Itto and supplied the fireworks. In Enchanted Tales of the Mikawa Festival (5.4) she worked with Sayu, Ayaka and the bake-danuki Kichiboushi.
